aliases: samples quenched after holding at 1100 °C for 3 min

summary: S1100 is the Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr low-density steel condition obtained by single-stage heat treatment — holding at 1100 °C for 3 min followed by quenching to room temperature — after the same upstream homogenization, hot rolling and air cooling applied to the whole alloy. It was produced "for comparison of tensile properties only": it shows the lowest strengths (YS 827 MPa, UTS 998 MPa at 25 °C) and the largest tensile ductility of the studied conditions, with the engineering stress–strain curve peaking just below 1000 MPa and extending furthest, to about 60 % strain, but it was not characterised microstructurally and was not impact tested.
composition: Nominal composition Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr (wt.%), with the analyzed ingot chemistry Fe-20.3Mn-8.6Al-1.4C-2.1Ni-2.9Cr (wt.%). Fe–Mn–C is the base system, into which Al is added to lower density (about 1.5 % density reduction per 1 wt% Al); the measured density of the steel is 6.78 g/cm³, roughly 14 % below that of pure iron (7.87 g/cm³). Ni is added to form the non-shearable B2 phase with Al, which improves strain work-hardening ability, and Cr is added to enhance corrosion resistance, to inhibit κ-carbide formation and to raise the soluble C content in austenite. The alloy itself was produced by vacuum induction melting. No separate composition measurement is reported specifically for S1100; the chemistry quoted is that of the common alloy ingot.
processing: Alloy melted by vacuum induction melting, then homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h, hot rolled at 1050–950 °C down to a 6 mm sheet, and air cooled to room temperature. S1100 is then the single-stage heat treatment branch of the schedule: the hot-rolled sheet is held at 1100 °C for 3 min and quenched to room temperature (water quench). This is the higher-temperature counterpart of the sibling single-stage conditions S1000 (1000 °C/3 min + quench) and S1050 (1050 °C/3 min + quench), and it lies outside the multi-stage heat treatment (MHT) route of 1000 °C/3 min quench → 750 °C/15 min quench → 1050 °C/3 min quench; it was run for comparison of tensile properties only.
